title: Mirabel and the Witness
premise: Orsen Dunmore is hired by a frightened woman, Mirabel Voss, who pays a fortune to prove her husband's murder hasn't happened yet — because she has seen the plan in his ledgers and knows the killer will strike within days. As Orsen investigates, he discovers the 'witness' everyone swears died years ago is alive, hidden, and the only person who can expose the conspiracy behind the planned killing — a conspiracy that reaches into Orsen's own firm. When the murder attempt comes early, Orsen must choose between protecting Mirabel, who turns out to be far more entangled than she claimed, and revealing the truth that will destroy them both. In the end, Orsen finds the witness, but saving him means sacrificing the career and reputation he built on never forgetting anything.
about_author: S. M. Kavanagh spent a decade working claims for an insurance company before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange, quiet tragedies of paperwork and payout. They live in a coastal town where fog rolls in most mornings, writing mysteries about people who know too much.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Orsen Dunmore, whose photographic memory makes him invaluable and isolated, takes an unusual case: Mirabel Voss pays triple to prove her husband hasn't been murdered yet. Her fear is precise, detailed, impossible to fake — or so it seems. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: wary fascination curdling into unease as he realizes he wants the job more than he should.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Digging through Aldous Voss's business records, Orsen finds payments funneled to a name officially dead for six years: Elias Crane, the witness to a fire that killed eleven workers. Someone at Orsen's own firm signed off on the original settlement. POV: Orsen, with a brief interlude from Mirabel's diary entries. Emotional beat: dread deepening as loyalty to his profession collides with what the evidence demands.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen tracks Crane to a river town and finds him alive but broken, guarded by a nurse who owes him everything. Before Orsen can move him, assassins arrive — the murder plot accelerating beyond its schedule. Mirabel appears, and Orsen realizes she orchestrated his involvement to flush out Crane. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: betrayal and adrenaline fused; the climax begins as they flee under gunfire.

chapters.title: A Memory Worth Burning
chapters.summary: Cornered, Orsen uses his perfect recall to reconstruct the fire's true timeline from fragments only he retained, exposing the firm's corruption and Mirabel's coerced role in it. Crane testifies; Aldous Voss is arrested before the murder can happen. Orsen burns his own clean record to do it. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: costly resolution — truth won, survival redefined, and Mirabel walking away free while he carries the price.
